infos.meta_title: Practical info – Getting to Ios | To Spiti Mas
infos.hero_text: Getting here, getting around, enjoying it
infos.route_text: Ios has no airport. You always arrive by sea, and that is where the holiday begins.
infos.step1_text: Fly into Athens, or straight to a nearby island: Santorini, Naxos, Paros, Mykonos or Milos.
infos.step2_text: From Santorini, Ios is 35 minutes by fast boat. From Piraeus, allow 4 hours by fast boat and 7 to 8 hours by conventional ferry.
infos.step3_text2: The boat docks at the port of Ios (Ormos). The house is about 15 minutes on foot or 5 minutes by taxi.
infos.airports_text: Shortest crossing times by fast boat. Conventional ferries are slower and cheaper.
infos.ap_athens_ferry: Via Piraeus or Rafina, see below
infos.airlines: Flights to Naxos, Paros and Milos from Athens: Olympic Air and Sky Express. Flights to Santorini and Mykonos from all over Europe, including with Aegean Airlines.
infos.piraeus_1: Duration 4 h 10 min by fast boat, 7 to 8 h by conventional ferry
infos.piraeus_3: Frequency all year round, almost every day
infos.piraeus_4: From the airport metro line 3 with no change (about 1 h), X96 bus (1 h to 1 h 30 min, day and night) or taxi
infos.rafina_3: Frequency in season, roughly May to October
infos.rafina_4: From the airport the closest port: 20 minutes by taxi, or KTEL bus (about 30 min)
infos.ferry_notice: Book your tickets on Ferryhopper or directly with the operators. In July and August, the meltemi wind can delay or cancel sailings, so allow a spare day before your flight home.
infos.bus_1: Main route Port, Chora, Mylopotas. In summer, buses run very frequently.
infos.bus_2: Remote beaches Manganari, Agia Theodoti, Psathi: one or two services a day in summer
infos.bus_3: 2026 fares €2.20 to Chora, Mylopotas or Koumbara, €4.50 to Manganari
infos.bus_4: Tickets from the machines at the bus station by the port
infos.taxi_hint: There are few taxis on the island. In high season, book the day before for your arrival and departure.
infos.rental_text: Several rental companies are based at the port. A car is useful for the wild beaches in the south and east. A private parking space awaits you at the house.
infos.walk_text: An old cobbled path climbs from the port to Chora: 1.2 km and 20 to 25 minutes uphill. Wear good shoes and avoid the hottest hours.
infos.money_notice2: Cash machines and supermarkets at the port and in Chora. The nearest to the house: the Mini Market on Yalos beach, 5 minutes on foot, and the Aegean Market at the port, open every day from 8 am to 9.30 pm, 10 minutes away.
infos.climate_text: The season runs from May to October. June and September bring warm sea and fewer people. April, May and October are perfect for walking.
infos.climate_caption: Average temperatures on Ios, in degrees Celsius
infos.meltemi: The meltemi, a dry and steady north wind, blows mostly in July and August. It cools the hot days. On very windy days, choose the southern beaches such as Manganari.
infos.updated: Information checked in November 2026. Boat and bus timetables change every season, so please check them before you travel.
infos.meta_desc: How to get to Ios: nearby airports, ferries from Athens and the islands, buses and taxis on the island, useful numbers and climate.

ios.meta_title: Ios & Kampos – Our island guide | To Spiti Mas
ios.kampos_lead: Kampos means “the countryside”: a quiet hillside between the port and Skarkos hill, facing Chora.
ios.kampos_p1: From the house, Yalos beach is 5 minutes on foot and the port about fifteen. Skarkos hill and its ancient site are 15 minutes' walk away. Chora, the hilltop village, is reached by bus, by taxi or along the old cobbled path.
ios.kampos_p2: Here are the places we love and recommend to our guests.
ios.map_note: The map shows the neighbourhood. We send you the exact address with your booking confirmation.
ios.chora_text: The white village and its alleys, the windmills on the ridge and the church of Panagia Gremiotissa at the very top. The best spot on the island for the sunset.
ios.skarkos_text: A Bronze Age settlement, one of the most important in the Cyclades, 15 minutes' walk from the house. Its finds are on display at the archaeological museum in Chora.
ios.theatre_text: An ancient-style marble amphitheatre just behind the windmills. It hosts concerts in summer, facing the sea.
ios.homer_text: In the north of the island, above Plakotos. Legend has it that Homer died on Ios. The sea view alone is worth the trip.
ios.paleokastro_text: The ruins of a Venetian castle in the east of the island, between Agia Theodoti and Psathi, with spectacular views.
ios.port_text: Caiques and nets on the quay, a few minutes from the house. In the morning, you can buy the fish that will end up on the plancha.
ios.beaches_text: In summer, the meltemi blows from the north. On very windy days, choose a sheltered beach in the south.
ios.yalos_text: Our beach, 5 minutes' walk away. Long, sandy, shallow and well equipped, with tavernas and beach bars.
ios.mylopotas_text: The island's large bay, well equipped, with water sports and a party atmosphere. Served by frequent buses.
ios.manganari_text: In the south, a string of turquoise coves sheltered from the meltemi. The most beautiful on the island, many say.
ios.koumbara_text: In the west, facing Sikinos. Exposed to the wind, but superb at the end of the day.
ios.theodoti_text: In the north-east, at the end of a scenic road. A large, peaceful beach and tavernas right on the sand.
ios.wild_text: The wild beaches of the east and south-east, with no facilities at all. For a timeless day out, with a car and a picnic basket.
ios.addresses_text2: The restaurants, bars and shops we recommend. Most of them open from May to October.
ios.addr_octopus: The Octopus Tree, Yalos harbour the closest to the house. Grilled octopus, meze and courgette fritters by the water.
ios.addr_katogi: Katogi, Chora meze in a lovely courtyard. Try the pasta salad with local cheese. Book a few days ahead.
ios.addr_byron: Lord Byron, Chora a mezedopoleio with a bohemian feel, a safe bet for years.
ios.addr_drakos: Drakos, Mylopotas charcoal-grilled fish at the end of the beach, since 1963.
ios.addr_ithaka: Ithaka, port more modern Mediterranean cooking, such as octopus on fava purée.
ios.addr_iosclub: Ios Club, Chora on the ridge above the port since 1968. Classical music and cocktails while the sun goes down.
ios.addr_steps: Steps Bar, Chora a drink on cushion-covered steps, below the windmills.
ios.addr_pathos: Pathos, Koumbara a lounge restaurant on the hill, facing the sunset.
ios.addr_skotiri: Skotiri the cheese of Ios, fresh and tangy, matured in a goatskin bag with thyme and savory. You will find it on almost every table.
ios.addr_diaseli: Diaseli cheese dairy, north of the island a family cheese dairy with a small museum and tastings.
ios.addr_mosenta: Mosenta thyme honey, island cheeses, pasteli and jams.
ios.addr_food_1: The fishing harbour fresh fish in the morning, when the boats come in
ios.addr_food_3b: Mini Market and Aegean Market the closest to the house, on Yalos beach and at the port
ios.addr_boat: Boat trip around the island boats leave from Yalos harbour for the southern beaches, which you cannot reach by road.
ios.addr_adventure: Ios Adventure, Chora guided walks, as far as the Diaseli cheese dairy, and e-bike rides to Homer's tomb.
ios.addr_dive: Diving, kayaking and paddleboarding, Mylopotas the Meltemi Dive and New Dive centres, on the beach.
ios.addr_rental: Car or scooter hire several rental companies at the port and in Chora
ios.addr_notice: Opening hours change every season: call or book before you go, especially in July and August.
ios.hike_title: On foot, by boat, at sunset
ios.hike_p1: The Ios Paths project has restored waymarked trails across the island. From the house, the Yalos, Skarkos, Chora loop and back is about 4 km: it is our favourite late-afternoon walk.
ios.hike_p2: For sunsets, climb up to the windmills of Chora or to the church of Panagia Gremiotissa. In summer, don't miss a village festival, the panigiri: music, dancing and a shared meal until late into the night.
ios.trips_text: Ios lies at the heart of the Cyclades. Times are for fast boats. Check the seasonal timetables before you go.
ios.trip_sikinos_why: The closest and most authentic, with no crowds.
ios.trip_santorini_why: The caldera and the villages of Oia and Fira.
ios.trip_folegandros_why: One of the most beautiful Choras in the Cyclades, on the edge of a cliff.
ios.trip_naxos_why: The Portara, the mountain villages and the long beaches.
ios.trip_paros_why: Naoussa, Parikia and their alleys. Best with a night there.
ios.cta_text: Planes, ferries, buses and taxis: everything you need to know to reach the house.
ios.meta_desc: Our guide to Ios: Kampos, Chora, the most beautiful beaches, walks, our favourite places and day trips to the neighbouring islands.

house.meta_title: The house – To Spiti Mas, Ios
house.hero_text: A Cycladic escape in the heart of Ios
house.intro_title: A house designed to experience Ios differently
house.intro_lead: Set slightly above Yalos beach, 400 metres away, the house looks out over Chora, the port and the Kampos countryside.
house.intro_p1: The village and its buzz are a few minutes away, but here all is calm. In the morning, you walk down to the beach. In the evening, you watch the lights of Chora come on from the terrace.
house.intro_p2b: You have the whole house to yourselves, with no locked rooms, and its large outdoor spaces facing the Aegean Sea.
house.archi_lead: A new house, built in the island's tradition.
house.archi_p1: Whitewashed walls, arches, pergolas and dry-stone walls echo the style of the houses of Ios.
house.archi_p2: The materials are those of the past: marble, wood, polished concrete and painted cement. They keep the house cool and play with the light from morning to evening.
house.terraces_text: A large lounge for drinks and long evenings, a dining area in the shade of the pergola, a summer kitchen with a plancha for grilling the fisherman's catch, a hanging bed rocked by the Cycladic breeze and a sun terrace with eight loungers.
house.garden_p1: Fig trees, pomegranates, cacti and bougainvillea make up a typical Cycladic dry garden, fully enclosed.
house.garden_p2c: On your way back from the beach, an outdoor shower awaits in the garden. In the evening, soft lights glow on the stone walls. A private parking space is kept for your car.
house.rooms_text3: Five beds across three bedrooms. Two bedrooms have their own bathroom; the third shares the common bathroom. A single bed in the lounge corner welcomes an eighth guest.
house.room1_text2: The brightest room, with windows open to the view.
house.room1_view: View of Chora and the port
house.room2_text: More earthy and intimate, with niches carved into the wall and soft light.
house.room3_text2: Perfect for a family: children love climbing up to the mezzanine.
house.living_p1b: A fully equipped kitchen opens onto the dining room. Enough to cook for eight, even on evenings when the wind is too strong to dine outside.
house.living_p2b: Under the stairs, a lounge corner with a TV is made for reading or a nap. After dark, soft lighting takes over.
house.living_p3: A shared bathroom in polished concrete, with its curved-wall shower, completes the common rooms.
house.no_ac: The house has no air conditioning. Its thick walls, ceiling fans and the Cycladic breeze keep it cool in summer.
house.reviews_score: Rated 4.9 out of 5 by 29 guests on Airbnb.
house.review_lilian: “Martial's house is absolutely perfect. Well located: 5 minutes on foot from the port and the beach, yet away from the bustle. Nicely decorated, comfortable, with a view of the bay: wonderful. An unforgettable stay.”
house.review_madeleine: “This house is a magnificent vacation home. Everything about it was great. The house was very clean and the beds very comfortable. The outdoor seating area is a fabulous lounging area and a wonderful place to admire the incredible sunsets.”
